claims.text: The starting coating is a nanoscale multilayer with alternating FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The starting HEA layers possess substantial compositional complexity.
The starting multilayer exhibits severe lattice distortion.
The starting multilayer has established short-range order at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Changing interlayer composition through sputtering can modulate interfacial lattice distortion and short-range order.
A suitable composition change will simultaneously increase interfacial lattice distortion and disrupt short-range order.
Interfacial short-range order and lattice distortion govern the creep behavior of FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
Pronounced short-range order impedes dislocation motion.
Lower lattice distortion combined with pronounced short-range order produces a dislocation-mediated creep regime.
Increasing interfacial lattice distortion progressively destroys short-range order.
Disruption of short-range order facilitates atomic diffusion.
Increasing interfacial lattice distortion and reducing short-range order shifts the dominant creep mechanism from dislocation-mediated to diffusion-assisted plasticity.
Samples with enhanced interfacial lattice distortion and reduced short-range order will have higher creep strain rates than the baseline coating.
Enhanced-distortion samples will contain fewer persistent dislocation networks than the baseline.
Enhanced-distortion samples will show more microstructural evidence of diffusion-driven deformation than the baseline.
Standard-composition baseline coatings have relatively high interfacial short-range order, lower lattice distortion, and dislocation-dominant creep.
Temperature and applied stress determine whether time-dependent plasticity and different creep mechanisms are activated.
The proposed mechanism shift applies only while the nanoscale multilayer architecture is preserved.
Conditions causing phase transformation or coating delamination are outside the hypothesis's intended regime.
4D-STEM combined with mechanical testing can reveal loading-induced changes in short-range order and associated defect structures.
